evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said 'This should take within the next five to ten minutes of your time. Then we'll be able to build an accurate quote you can depend on sounds good.' — framing present but time estimate was 5–10 min, not the standard 10–15 min, and no clear wait for verbal yes before proceeding.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name: Julian; moving day: Next Saturday the 3rd; property type: apartment; moving within San Antonio (city-to-city route satisfied as same city). Size confirmed as one-bedroom apartment (second location two-bedroom). All four basics confirmed.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment); floors/stories (second floor, no elevator, stairs); number of rooms (one-bedroom, later two-bedroom destination); walking distance (half a minute from truck to stairs); special items (washer, dryer, bed, TV, couch); access concerns checked (none); fragile/valuable items checked (none). Full coverage across seven logistics categories.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep stated: 'So a typical number of boxes is between fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you feel that you fall within that range?' — box count range offered and customer affirmed.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: No recognizable version of 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' was asked.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provided: 'we'll send out to livers and one truck, estimated time is between three to four hours estimated cost would be $964.' — anchored to home size (one-bedroom to two-bedroom move, 25 minutes away, stairs at both ends) and personalized to this customer's specific move details.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee of $140 disclosed upfront ($103/hour per mover, $140 trip fee). Minimum of 2.5 hours and 15-minute increment prorating explained: 'We will then have us first, as long as you need us for any move we have a minimum of twenty and a half hours once you go over that it will always be prorated into fifteen minute increments.' Both components present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent. Call moved directly to Two Promises section without checking customer's reaction to pricing.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated: 'we have ontime guarantee we value your time. So, if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' — discount terms fully covered.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated: 'we have no worry, damage coverage included on the already way that you're paying us we will provide up to $2,000 per move that is to repair replace and reimburse for your items.' — $2,000 coverage and built-in framing stated, but no explicit 'no deductible / no fine print' language used.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar. No loop-closing question asked after Two Promises.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asked 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine final concerns check. Call ended without this step.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No recognizable version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' was asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any explicit ask for the business. Call ends abruptly after pricing quote without closing step.

top_strength: Systematic logistics probing — the rep gathered property type, floor/stories, room count, walking distance, special items, and access concerns comprehensively, which will support accurate estimate delivery and crew prep.
coaching_note: The call dropped off after pricing without any of the final three sections (concerns again, Two Promises loop-close, or explicit ask) — add a genuine final-concerns check and ask for the business plainly before the call ends.
